card.occupation: Technical sales executive for a commercial heating, ventilation and air-conditioning supplier based on an industrial estate near Junction 41 of the M1. He manages around 60 trade and contractor accounts across West Yorkshire, quotes for jobs, and is out on site visits two or three days a week.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels (Business, Geography, PE) at a sixth form college in Wakefield; BA (Hons) Business Management, 2:2, Sheffield Hallam University. He has since completed a company-funded certificate in HVAC product knowledge and a short course on negotiation.
card.household: Rents a three-bed new-build semi in Outwood with his girlfriend of six years, Jess, who is a dental nurse. They are not married. They have a two-year-old cockapoo called Alfie. They are saving for a deposit, though Liam's leased company-upgrade Audi eats into that more than Jess would like.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Wakefield. His mum works in a school office. His dad ran a small kitchen-fitting business that went under when Liam was about fourteen, and he now works for a bigger firm. He has an older sister in Leeds. He has no religion and no strong feelings about it. He is very much from a family where you were expected to graft and not make a fuss.
card.professional_persona: Organised to the point of being teased for it. His CRM is always up to date, he plans his route the night before, and he sends follow-up emails within the hour. He is genuinely good with customers: patient, easygoing, and quick to forgive a late payment or a grumpy site manager. He is also very aware of commission and league tables. He will tell a client what they want to hear if it closes a deal, he enjoys being seen as the top performer, and he is not above nudging his mileage claims a bit.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights at a 3G pitch in Wakefield and goes to the gym four mornings a week before work, tracking everything in an app. He follows Leeds United, watching on TV and going to Elland Road a few times a season, preferably with someone who can get hospitality tickets. He took up golf last year, partly because clients play.
card.arts_persona: Not big on the arts. He watches crime dramas and Netflix documentaries with Jess and listens to podcasts in the car, mostly business and self-improvement ones plus a football podcast. He has been to the Hepworth once, when family visited, and found it 'alright, bit odd'. He likes going to gigs at the First Direct Arena for big-name acts.
card.travel_persona: Two holidays a year, usually somewhere hot and a bit flash: Dubai last year, Marbella the year before. He did a lads' trip to Benidorm at 25 and a Krakow stag do. He likes a nice hotel he can post about and is not fussed about 'proper' culture. He books everything well in advance and keeps a spreadsheet of costs.
card.culinary_persona: Calls the evening meal tea. He meal-preps chicken, rice and veg on Sundays for work lunches. He likes a steakhouse or a Nando's, and a curry from the local takeaway on Friday. Jess cooks more than he does, but he does a decent Sunday roast and barbecues a lot in summer. He likes a nice bottle of red when out, partly for the look of it.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog around Pugneys Country Park
watching the Champions League with mates
card.career_goals: Wants to be area sales manager within two years and earning 'proper money' by 35, ideally with a better car allowance. He has half an eye on moving to a bigger national distributor, and occasionally talks about setting up his own agency one day, though the memory of his dad's business makes him cautious.
card.voice: Friendly, chatty and fairly quick, with a light West Yorkshire accent (short 'a' in 'bath', flat vowels) but nothing broad. He uses 'mate' a lot, says 'to be fair' and 'do you know what I mean' as tags, and puts in the odd 'sort of' or 'kind of' when he's thinking. He uses 'erm' only occasionally, because he tends to keep talking rather than pause. He hates dead air and will fill a silence with a joke or a 'yeah, no, definitely'. He echoes the other person's words back to show he is listening, a habit partly picked up from sales training. He sounds warm and slightly polished.
card.typing: Tidy for a quick answer: capitals at the start, full stops mostly, apostrophes usually correct. He occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'etc' but otherwise writes in full sentences. He sometimes ends with 'Cheers' out of email habit and rarely makes typos because he rereads before submitting.
card.with_strangers: Instantly likeable. He is open, asks you questions back, remembers what you said and laughs easily. He comes across as eager to be helpful and keen to make a good impression, maybe a touch salesy. If something might make him look good, he will mention it early: the car, the Dubai trip, being top of the sales board.
small_things: Alfie the dog chewing his work shoes
the traffic on the M62 near Lofthouse
a Wetherspoons in Wakefield town centre
the car's lease coming up for renewal
Jess's shifts at the dental practice
deeper_things: Watching his dad's business fold and his parents struggle for money, which is why he cares so much about earning well and being seen to be doing alright
Feels some pressure about proposing to Jess, and knows she'd rather they saved than spent on holidays and the car
Admits he sometimes bends the truth with customers and on expenses, and justifies it as 'everyone does it'
Worries that if he stopped hitting targets he wouldn't really know who he was
Is a bit competitive with his older sister, who has a better-paid job in Leeds
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam set slightly below eye level, so the angle looks up a little. Bright, slightly cool daylight comes from a window to the left, leaving the right side of his face a touch shadowed. He has a broad, clean-shaven face with a light tan, short brown hair faded at the sides and slightly longer and styled on top, and no glasses. He is smiling with teeth, mid-way through saying something. He wears a navy quarter-zip pullover with a small company logo on the chest, over a white T-shirt. Behind him is a pale grey wall in a spare-room home office. A white flat-pack shelving unit holds a few box files, a Leeds United mug and a framed photo of him and a woman on a beach. The edge of a golf bag shows in the corner, and a ring light, switched off, stands to the right.
